transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
U.S. officials are trying to calm public health fears
over a controlled detonation in the morning in Iowa.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports the Army and multiple agencies
have held a public briefing about the plan
to destroy an explosive stockpile in Middletown.
>> The possible toxic fallout from detonating a stockpile
of unstable explosives has raised concerns for people
and livestock, some of whom have been advised to evacuate.
At the briefing, Army Major General Eric Shirley said
the ordnance could explode spontaneously if it's not destroyed now.
>> We know and are confident and have the full concurrence
of all the agencies who have been participating in this,
that the controlled detonation is absolutely the only way to go.
>> This comes after days of confusion
and President Trump saying he would blame
the incoming Democratic governor-elect of Iowa for any harm
if the explosion were delayed.
The Army has been aware of the danger since March
and later discarded a plan to use chemicals
to neutralize the stockpile.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
>> Now to Utah, where the state attorney general's office
is asking a court to dismiss criminal charges
against prediction market firm Kalshi.
From member station KUER, Hugo Ricker Bell reports.
>> In the original charges, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown
alleged Kalshi had continued to operate in Utah
even after it was banned.
But yesterday, the predictive market site
pulled itself out of the Utah market.
>> Now at this point, they have made it clear
that they are no longer operating in the state of Utah
and our investigators have verified that.
And so at least for now, we've agreed to drop these charges.
>> It's the latest in the legal tennis match
over what constitutes gambling.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has also sued Utah
to block it from enforcing its state anti-gambling laws.
There's also an ongoing civil suit
that has Utah asking for damages to be paid by Kalshi.
For NPR News, I'm Hugo Ricker Bell in Salt Lake City.
>> Medicare has unveiled its latest round
of discounted drug prices for beneficiaries.
The lower prices for 13 drugs will take effect in January.
Here's NPR's Sydney Lupkin.
>> Medicare says it negotiated an 84% discount
on Eli Lilly's popular type 2 diabetes drug, Trulicity.
That puts it at $150 a month.
Trulicity is an older GLP-1 drug,
and unlike Lilly's ZEPBOUND, it's not approved for weight loss.
But the Medicare price for Trulicity is lower than the $245
the White House negotiated for newer GLP-1s, including Ozempic.
Medicare also negotiated discounts for drugs that treat HIV,
various cancers, and inflammatory conditions like Crohn's disease.
This is the third round of Medicare drug price negotiations
and the first to include intravenous drugs
covered by Medicare Part B.
Overall, the program has negotiated the prices of 37 drugs
since it started in August of 2023.
Sydney Lupkin, NPR News.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
A deadly plane crashed Tuesday off the coast of Mississippi.
The U.S. Coast Guard says six people, including two young boys,
have been found dead after their Cessna 210 went down
in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula and Horn Island,
part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore.
The Federal Aviation Administration
and the National Transportation Safety Board
are expected to investigate the crash.
A joint European-Japanese mission has successfully launched
into orbit around the planet Mercury.
But Joe Palko reports things did not go exactly as planned.
>> The mission is called Bepi Colombo.
It's actually made up of two probes,
a Japanese-built orbiter for studying Mercury's magnetic field
and a European orbiter for studying the planet's surface features and chemistry.
On Saturday, November 21, when Bepi Colombo was just 400 miles from the planet,
the main engine fired right on time,
but later analysis showed the engine cut off unexpectedly,
putting the spacecraft into an orbit further from the planet than intended.
Mission managers are still determining exactly why this happened,
but they say they can still achieve all of the mission's planned scientific objectives.
For NPR News, I'm Joe Palko.
>> Pakistan's first astronaut in orbit
is now the first foreign astronaut to board China's space station.
China's state broadcaster says Sichuan Ali and two Chinese astronauts
entered the station a short time ago having docked their Xinzhou-24 spacecraft
after three and a half hours after launch,
a joint flight part of an agreement signed by China and Pakistan in 2025.
This is NPR.
plus dot NPR dot org.

topics.text: U.S. Army plans controlled detonation of explosive stockpile in Middletown, Iowa, despite public health fears
Utah attorney general moves to drop criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi after it exits state
Medicare unveils discounted prices for 13 drugs, including Eli Lilly's Trulicity, effective January
Coast Guard finds six dead after Cessna 210 crashes in Gulf of Mexico off Mississippi coast
Joint European-Japanese BepiColombo spacecraft enters Mercury orbit, but engine cutoff leaves it in wrong orbit
Pakistani astronaut becomes first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station
